Definition: a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitants of Tarpel, a place in Assyria
BiblicalUsage: The Tarpelites were a group of colonists planted in the cities of Samaria after the northern kingdom was carried away. They are named among the writers of the letter to Artaxerxes against the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the letter-writers show how the enemies of God's work band together, and the Tarpelites' name is kept in the record of their opposition.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
